title: Chemical Bonding: Hybridisation and Spatial Geometry
subject: Chemistry
scope_summary: Authored Grade 11 Chemical Bonding and Hybridisation spine covering electron-domain counting, localized Valence Bond hybridisation (sp, sp2, sp3), sigma and pi decomposition, orthogonal unhybridised p-orbital overlap, and the distinction between electron-domain geometry and molecular shape.

buckets.title: Chemical Bonding and Hybridisation
buckets.badge_reason: Introductory hybridisation requires separating electron domain count from shared pairs, identifying unhybridised p orbitals, and distinguishing domain geometry from molecular shape.

conventions.statement: Count electron domains before assigning hybridisation; double and triple bonds each count as one domain.

scope.covers: Grade 11 introductory chemical bonding, VSEPR domain counting, sp, sp2, sp3 hybridisation, sigma/pi decomposition, ethene/CO2/HCN models.

microtopics.title: Electron-Domain Counting and Molecular Shape Geometry
microtopics.badge_reason: Distinguishing electron-domain geometry from molecular shape across molecules with central lone pairs.
microtopics.inferential_jump: CH4, NH3, H2O have four introductory domains but tetrahedral, pyramidal and bent nuclear shapes respectively.

teaching_path.action: Inventory bonds and central lone pairs separately.
teaching_path.why_valid: The givens supply three bonds at each centre but different lone-pair counts.
inputs: BF3 and NH3 each have three sigma bonds to the central atom. BF3 has no central lone pair; NH3 has one. Explain why three sigma bonds alone cannot determine the same central hybridisation and molecular shape for both.
teaching_path.output: BF3: 3+0=3 domains; NH3: 3+1=4.

teaching_path.action: Apply the bounded introductory domain models.
teaching_path.why_valid: The local total, rather than bonds alone, selects the model arrangement.
inputs: BF3: 3+0=3 domains; NH3: 3+1=4.
teaching_path.output: BF3: planar/sp2; NH3: tetrahedral domains/sp3-like.

teaching_path.action: Name shape using bonded nuclei only.
teaching_path.why_valid: The N lone-pair domain has no bonded nucleus.
inputs: BF3: planar/sp2; NH3: tetrahedral domains/sp3-like.
teaching_path.output: BF3 is trigonal planar; NH3 is trigonal pyramidal.

teaching_path.action: Compare NH3 with H2O.
teaching_path.why_valid: Three-bond/one-pair and two-bond/two-pair inventories both total four.
inputs: BF3 is trigonal planar; NH3 is trigonal pyramidal.
teaching_path.output: The same domain total can give different bonded-nucleus shapes.

teaching_path.action: Hold the claimed three-sigma condition fixed.
teaching_path.why_valid: Both supplied centres satisfy it, so an omitted lone-pair condition can test the implication.
inputs: Consider the claim: 'Any central atom with three sigma bonds must be sp2.' Given BF3: three B–F sigma bonds, zero boron lone pairs, planar; NH3: three N–H sigma bonds, one nitrogen lone pair, pyramidal. Decide whether these observations support the claim, give the decisive warrant, and state a more defensible introductory rule. Explain what the shape observations alone do not prove about orbitals.
teaching_path.output: BF3 and NH3 both have three sigma bonds.

teaching_path.action: Use nitrogen as the counterexample.
teaching_path.why_valid: NH3 also has one central lone pair; its local total is four.
inputs: BF3 and NH3 both have three sigma bonds.
teaching_path.output: Three sigma bonds alone do not imply three domains/sp2.

teaching_path.action: Replace the claim with a conditional local rule.
teaching_path.why_valid: Within localized introductory classification, bonds plus central lone pairs determine the domain total.
inputs: Three sigma bonds alone do not imply three domains/sp2.
teaching_path.output: Use the full inventory: three domains -> sp2 model; four -> sp3-like model.

teaching_path.action: Separate shape observations from a unique orbital basis.
teaching_path.why_valid: Nuclear geometry constrains a description but does not measure hybrid coefficients.
inputs: Use the full inventory: three domains -> sp2 model; four -> sp3-like model.
teaching_path.output: The counterexample rejects the bond-only rule without proving unique physical hybrid orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Recount carbon neighbours after H-to-F substitution.
teaching_path.why_valid: CH3F has three H and one F directly attached to C.
inputs: In CH3F, carbon has three C–H single bonds and one C–F single bond. Assign its introductory local hybridisation and explain why the number of electron-domain directions is unchanged from CH4 even though the attached atoms are different. Do not assume all bond properties are identical.
teaching_path.output: Four carbon bonding directions.

teaching_path.action: Apply the same local four-domain allocation.
teaching_path.why_valid: Changing substituent identity does not itself create a new neighbour or lone pair at C.
inputs: Four carbon bonding directions.
teaching_path.output: Introductory sp3 carbon model.

teaching_path.action: State what the count leaves open.
teaching_path.why_valid: Bond lengths, polarity and exact angles require information beyond neighbour counting.
inputs: Introductory sp3 carbon model.
teaching_path.output: No equality of C-H and C-F properties is inferred.

teaching_path.action: Test CH2F2 as a changed inventory.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two H and two F are still four neighbours.
inputs: No equality of C-H and C-F properties is inferred.
teaching_path.output: Four domains remain; electronegativity is not an extra domain.

teaching_path.action: Make atom-local inventories in CH3NH2.
teaching_path.why_valid: C has four single bonds; N has three single bonds and one lone pair.
inputs: For methylamine, CH3–NH2, carbon has four single bonds and nitrogen has three single bonds plus a lone pair. Compare the introductory local hybridisation and arrangement of bonded atoms at carbon and nitrogen. Explain why the same hybridisation label does not require identical molecular shapes.
teaching_path.output: C: 4+0; N: 3+1; both total four domains.

teaching_path.action: Assign the localized introductory domain models.
teaching_path.why_valid: Each four-domain centre can use sp3-like accounting under the stated local model.
inputs: C: 4+0; N: 3+1; both total four domains.
teaching_path.output: Four model directions at each centre.

teaching_path.action: Count nuclei for the separate shape descriptions.
teaching_path.why_valid: C has four bonded neighbours while N has three; a lone pair is not an atomic vertex.
inputs: Four model directions at each centre.
teaching_path.output: Tetrahedral C nuclear arrangement; pyramidal N arrangement.

teaching_path.action: Replace an N-H bond with an N-CH3 bond in a neutral amine comparison.
teaching_path.why_valid: The N inventory stays three bonds plus one lone pair.
inputs: Tetrahedral C nuclear arrangement; pyramidal N arrangement.
teaching_path.output: Local N count and pyramidal introductory description persist; exact angle is unresolved.

teaching_path.action: Hold the four-domain total fixed across three cases.
teaching_path.why_valid: CH4, NH3 and H2O have respective bond/pair inventories 4/0, 3/1 and 2/2.
inputs: A student says, 'If the electron-domain geometry is tetrahedral, the atoms must form a tetrahedral molecular shape.' Evaluate the statement using CH4, NH3 and H2O, with their respective central lone-pair counts of zero, one and two.
teaching_path.output: All have four introductory domains.

teaching_path.action: Use all domains for domain geometry.
teaching_path.why_valid: Bonding and lone-pair entries occupy the domain-model directions.
inputs: All have four introductory domains.
teaching_path.output: Tetrahedral electron-domain arrangement in all three.

teaching_path.action: Use bonded nuclei for molecular shape.
teaching_path.why_valid: Removing LP entries from the shape name changes the number of atomic vertices.
inputs: Tetrahedral electron-domain arrangement in all three.
teaching_path.output: CH4 tetrahedral; NH3 pyramidal; H2O bent.

teaching_path.action: State the condition for the two names to coincide.
teaching_path.why_valid: When there is no central lone pair every domain direction terminates at a bonded nucleus.
inputs: CH4 tetrahedral; NH3 pyramidal; H2O bent.
teaching_path.output: The student claim holds for the no-lone-pair case, not universally.

predict.prompt: A car cruises at a steady speed along a straight, level road with its engine running. Must the forward driving force be larger than the backward resistance just to keep it moving?
predict.defensible_answer: No. At steady velocity the net force is zero, so the forward and backward forces are equal in size.

attempt.produces: The total resistive force on the car with its direction, the net force on the car, and the car's velocity 10 s later, each justified from the steady 25 m/s.

rubric.criterion: Identify domain count: 3 domains for C2H4 (sp2) vs 2 domains for CO2 (sp).
Relate sp2 to trigonal planar (120°) and sp to linear (180°).
Explain that ethene has 1 pi bond while CO2 has 2 orthogonal pi bonds.
rubric.evidence_of: Understanding orthogonal unhybridised p orbital overlap.

accepted: The velocity is not changing, so the net force is zero and the resistive forces total 2000 N backward. With nothing changed, the car is still moving at 25 m/s in the same direction 10 s later.
rejected: 'The driving force must be bigger than the resistance, or the car would slow down.' At steady speed the net force is zero, so the two forces are equal.
'With zero net force the car is at rest 10 s later.' Zero net force keeps the velocity unchanged; it does not stop the car.

task.prompt: A 1500 kg car cruises at a steady 25 m/s along a straight, level road. The road pushes it forward with a driving force of 2000 N. Find the total resistive force and the net force on the car, and say what its velocity will be 10 s later if nothing changes.
givens: Mass 1500 kg; speed a steady 25 m/s in a straight line.
Resistive forces (air and rolling) act backward.

route.ask: What does 'a steady 25 m/s in a straight line' tell you about the car's acceleration?
route.why_this_ask: It separates 'is moving' from 'is changing its motion' before any force is discussed.

route.ask: So what must the net force on the car be?
route.why_this_ask: The net-force value is derived from the unchanged velocity, not assumed from the speed.

route.ask: The road pushes forward with 2000 N. What total backward force makes the net force zero?
route.why_this_ask: It finds the unknown resistance from the balance.

route.ask: If nothing changes for 10 s, can the velocity change? What is it then?
route.why_this_ask: It identifies unchanged velocity, not rest, as what zero net force keeps.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The teaching path compares a released moving cart with a resting cart. The learner route starts from the car's steady speed, derives the zero net force from it, and uses that to find the unknown resistance and the later velocity.

boundary_test.prompt: The driver eases off and the driving force drops to 500 N while the resistance is still 2000 N. Is the net force still zero, and what happens to the speed?
boundary_test.answer: No. The net force is 2000 − 500 = 1500 N backward, so the car slows at 1500/1500 = 1 m/s². Zero net force described only the steady interval.
boundary_test.confirms: Zero net force goes with unchanged velocity, not with motion as such.

teaching_path.action: Count C neighbours in HCHO.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two H and one O are three connections; bond multiplicity is a separate inventory.
inputs: For H2C=O, assign the carbon hybridisation, count the sigma and pi components of the C=O bond, and identify the carbon orbital left available for the pi component. Keep electron-domain counting separate from counting shared electron pairs.
teaching_path.output: Three domains; no C lone pair.

teaching_path.action: Allocate the four carbon valence functions.
teaching_path.why_valid: One 2s plus two 2p form three sp2 hybrids, leaving the third 2p unused in that mixing.
inputs: Three domains; no C lone pair.
teaching_path.output: Three sigma-direction hybrids plus one residual p.

teaching_path.action: Resolve the C=O bond components.
teaching_path.why_valid: A localized double-bond account has one axial sigma and one lateral pi component.
inputs: Three sigma-direction hybrids plus one residual p.
teaching_path.output: C=O: one sigma + one pi; residual C p supplies the pi role.

teaching_path.action: Close the basis ledger using an sp comparison.
teaching_path.why_valid: sp gives two hybrids and two residual p functions from the same four inputs.
inputs: C=O: one sigma + one pi; residual C p supplies the pi role.
teaching_path.output: Both allocations total four; no p function is spent twice.

teaching_path.action: Build the two local carbon sigma frames.
teaching_path.why_valid: Each ethene carbon has three sigma directions and one remaining p function in sp2 accounting.
inputs: Ethene is H2C=CH2. Translate this Lewis representation into a qualitative orbital-overlap diagram showing the C–C sigma framework, the two unhybridised carbon p orbitals and their side-on overlap. Label which directions are in the molecular plane and which are perpendicular to it.
teaching_path.output: Two in-plane three-direction frames; one perpendicular p at each C.

teaching_path.action: Align the p functions relative to the molecular plane.
teaching_path.why_valid: A residual p is perpendicular to its carbon sigma plane.
inputs: Two in-plane three-direction frames; one perpendicular p at each C.
teaching_path.output: Parallel perpendicular p directions in planar ethene.

teaching_path.action: Draw both axial and lateral overlap.
teaching_path.why_valid: The C-C sigma component is axial; lateral p overlap lies above and below the plane.
inputs: Parallel perpendicular p directions in planar ethene.
teaching_path.output: A sigma framework plus a pi component with a node in the molecular plane.

teaching_path.action: Compare rigid rotation with relative CH2-group rotation.
teaching_path.why_valid: Only the latter changes relative p alignment.
inputs: A sigma framework plus a pi component with a node in the molecular plane.
teaching_path.output: Whole-picture rotation preserves overlap geometry; relative twisting can reduce pi alignment.

teaching_path.action: Count two O neighbours at CO2 carbon.
teaching_path.why_valid: Each C=O multiple bond contributes one local direction.
inputs: For CO2, connect the central-carbon Lewis domain count to its hybrid-orbital model, the number of remaining carbon p orbitals and the sigma/pi composition of its two C=O bonds. Explain how these pieces fit one consistent linear arrangement.
teaching_path.output: Two carbon domains; linear introductory framework.

teaching_path.action: Allocate carbon orbitals without duplication.
teaching_path.why_valid: One 2s plus one 2p yields two sp hybrids; two p directions remain perpendicular.
inputs: Two carbon domains; linear introductory framework.
teaching_path.output: Two sigma directions and two residual C p functions.

teaching_path.action: Account for each localized C=O component.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two double bonds require two sigma and two pi components in this bookkeeping model.
inputs: Two sigma directions and two residual C p functions.
teaching_path.output: Two sigma + two pi; all four carbon functions have declared roles.

teaching_path.action: Bound the inference about terminal oxygen.
teaching_path.why_valid: A localized basis drawing is one representation of the electronic description; carbon counting does not uniquely measure an oxygen basis.
inputs: Two sigma + two pi; all four carbon functions have declared roles.
teaching_path.output: Linear carbon accounting is consistent; a unique observed O orbital-plane picture is not established.

teaching_path.action: Inventory carbon and nitrogen separately in HCN.
teaching_path.why_valid: C has H and N neighbours; N has one C neighbour plus one lone pair.
inputs: HCN is represented as H–C≡N with a lone pair on nitrogen. Assign the introductory hybridisation at carbon and nitrogen, and count the sigma and pi components of the C≡N bond. Explain how the local domain count is compatible with those components.
teaching_path.output: C: two domains; N: two domains.

teaching_path.action: Allocate each local four-function valence basis.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two sp hybrids leave two perpendicular p functions at each second-period centre.
inputs: C: two domains; N: two domains.
teaching_path.output: Introductory sp at C and N.

teaching_path.action: Count triple-bond components without adding local directions.
teaching_path.why_valid: Axial overlap gives one sigma; the two residual p pairs give two pi components.
inputs: Introductory sp at C and N.
teaching_path.output: C-N: one sigma + two pi; C-H adds one sigma.

teaching_path.action: Close the ten-valence-electron inventory.
teaching_path.why_valid: H+C+N contributes 1+4+5=10; four shared pairs and one N lone pair use five pairs.
inputs: C-N: one sigma + two pi; C-H adds one sigma.
teaching_path.output: Eight bonding electrons + two lone-pair electrons = ten.

teaching_path.action: Start from four carbon valence-basis functions.
teaching_path.why_valid: The second-period basis is one 2s plus three 2p.
inputs: A carbon centre has three sigma-bond directions, no lone pair, and participates in one pi bond. Translate this description into a qualitative local orbital arrangement and check that the orbitals used in the sigma and pi parts have not been counted twice.
teaching_path.output: Four inputs; three sigma directions and one pi role required.

teaching_path.action: Mix only the functions assigned to sigma directions.
teaching_path.why_valid: One s plus two p makes three in-plane sp2 hybrids.
inputs: Four inputs; three sigma directions and one pi role required.
teaching_path.output: Three hybrids; one p remains outside the mixing.

teaching_path.action: Assign the residual p to the pi role.
teaching_path.why_valid: It is perpendicular to the sigma plane and can overlap laterally with a suitable neighbour.
inputs: Three hybrids; one p remains outside the mixing.
teaching_path.output: Three sigma hybrids + one residual perpendicular p.

teaching_path.action: Check against sp and sp3 allocations.
teaching_path.why_valid: Those alternatives account for two hybrids plus two p, or four hybrids plus zero p.
inputs: Three sigma hybrids + one residual perpendicular p.
teaching_path.output: All totals are four; no function is simultaneously a hybrid input and an extra residual p.

predict.prompt: A car cruises at a steady speed along a straight, level road with its engine running. Must the forward driving force be larger than the backward resistance just to keep it moving?
predict.defensible_answer: No. At steady velocity the net force is zero, so the forward and backward forces are equal in size.

attempt.produces: The total resistive force on the car with its direction, the net force on the car, and the car's velocity 10 s later, each justified from the steady 25 m/s.

rubric.criterion: Identify domain count: 3 domains for C2H4 (sp2) vs 2 domains for CO2 (sp).
Relate sp2 to trigonal planar (120°) and sp to linear (180°).
Explain that ethene has 1 pi bond while CO2 has 2 orthogonal pi bonds.
rubric.evidence_of: Understanding orthogonal unhybridised p orbital overlap.

accepted: The velocity is not changing, so the net force is zero and the resistive forces total 2000 N backward. With nothing changed, the car is still moving at 25 m/s in the same direction 10 s later.
rejected: 'The driving force must be bigger than the resistance, or the car would slow down.' At steady speed the net force is zero, so the two forces are equal.
'With zero net force the car is at rest 10 s later.' Zero net force keeps the velocity unchanged; it does not stop the car.

task.prompt: A 1500 kg car cruises at a steady 25 m/s along a straight, level road. The road pushes it forward with a driving force of 2000 N. Find the total resistive force and the net force on the car, and say what its velocity will be 10 s later if nothing changes.
givens: Mass 1500 kg; speed a steady 25 m/s in a straight line.
Resistive forces (air and rolling) act backward.

route.ask: What does 'a steady 25 m/s in a straight line' tell you about the car's acceleration?
route.why_this_ask: It separates 'is moving' from 'is changing its motion' before any force is discussed.

route.ask: So what must the net force on the car be?
route.why_this_ask: The net-force value is derived from the unchanged velocity, not assumed from the speed.

route.ask: The road pushes forward with 2000 N. What total backward force makes the net force zero?
route.why_this_ask: It finds the unknown resistance from the balance.

route.ask: If nothing changes for 10 s, can the velocity change? What is it then?
route.why_this_ask: It identifies unchanged velocity, not rest, as what zero net force keeps.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The teaching path compares a released moving cart with a resting cart. The learner route starts from the car's steady speed, derives the zero net force from it, and uses that to find the unknown resistance and the later velocity.

boundary_test.prompt: The driver eases off and the driving force drops to 500 N while the resistance is still 2000 N. Is the net force still zero, and what happens to the speed?
boundary_test.answer: No. The net force is 2000 − 500 = 1500 N backward, so the car slows at 1500/1500 = 1 m/s². Zero net force described only the steady interval.
boundary_test.confirms: Zero net force goes with unchanged velocity, not with motion as such.

teaching_routes.title: Reveal Grade-9 Newton-law spine with bounded friction/connection preparation and frame extension
entry_needs: Can tell whether an object's velocity is changing; the specific turning-point diagnostic from Motion is not a prerequisite.
learner_actions: Separate motion from change of motion.
Keep individual forces distinct from their net result.
Assign each force to the body on which it acts.
Determine friction direction from relative slip tendency.
Use signed net external force with F_net = m a.
Test static friction against its limit before using a limiting or kinetic formula.
Apply a common acceleration only when an active connection keeps the relevant separation fixed.
Use one common tension magnitude only under explicit ideal-string/redirection assumptions.
Derive the one-fixed-pulley acceleration relation from constant string length rather than a pulley-count rule.
Keep Newton-third-law partner forces on different bodies.
Use observer-frame/pseudo-force reasoning only when an explicit extension question demands it.
help_plan: Use a released low-friction cart for the first-law contrast.
Use two separate body inventories before any force equations.
For friction, ask for N and f_required before revealing any coefficient formula.
For connected bodies, ask what physical condition keeps the relative separation fixed.
For a string/pulley task, require the ideal assumptions and actual length equation before any tension or acceleration shortcut.
Use roadside versus accelerating-bus descriptions for the observer boundary.
teaching_routes.reveal_plan: Completed constructions are visible only after body ownership, contact state, connection model and any string geometry are declared; coefficient and constraint relations are never presented as unconditional apparatus formulas.

source_preferences.reason: The four rungs are authored here without promoting candidate-packet authority.

when_not_suitable: Do not treat accelerating-frame/pseudo-force reasoning as ordinary Grade-9 Standard syllabus content.
Do not infer momentum-conservation or collision content from the presence of Newton's laws.
Do not use the single-fixed-pulley relation for movable/compound pulley geometry.
Do not assume equal tension after an ideal-string or ideal-redirection assumption is broken.

teaching_routes.title: Elicit Grade-9 Newton-law spine with bounded friction/connection preparation and frame extension
entry_needs: Same intrinsic Grade-9 force-law coverage as Core1A; no inferred learner mastery and no turning-point prerequisite.
learner_actions: Predict whether zero net force can coexist with steady motion.
Build body-specific force inventories before combining forces.
Predict friction direction from contact slip tendency.
Use the net force to predict acceleration.
Decide whether a static contact can supply the required friction before selecting a coefficient equality.
Name the connection that justifies a common acceleration.
Earn one tension symbol by stating the ideal-string model.
Reconstruct the one-fixed-pulley acceleration relation from constant string length.
Separate Newton-third-law partners by body.
Enter observer-frame reconstruction only for explicit extension demand.
help_plan: Ask which body receives each force before naming any pairing rule.
Ask what friction value the no-slip equations require before asking about a coefficient limit.
Ask which relative separation is fixed before offering a common acceleration.
Ask which string segments actually change length before offering a pulley relation.
Ask whether a physical agent changed before introducing a pseudo-force.
teaching_routes.reveal_plan: Prediction, reconstruction, misconception diagnosis and boundary tests precede the closed reveal.

source_preferences.reason: Each elicitation cycle is authored specifically for the corresponding rung.

when_not_suitable: Do not substitute a declarative diagram for the learner's body-ownership decision.
Do not present pseudo-force/frame-choice content as ordinary Grade-9 Standard syllabus material.
Do not hand over mu N as the friction value before the learner decides the contact state.
Do not hand over equal tension or an acceleration ratio without the model/geometry that justifies it.
